following:
 Order
This common order shall govern disposal of M.A.No. 6376/2023 and 7506/2023 as both these
appeals are filed by against the common award dated 31/8/2023 passed by 14th Member, Motor
Accident Claims Trib
unal, Gwalior in Claim Case No. 164/2021,

whereby, the Claims Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 3,92,471/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition to complainant/injured Charan Singh Rawat, who sustained grievous injuries in road accident dated 26/11/2020 and liability for payment of compensation amount was fastened over Driver-cum-Owner and Insurance Company jointly and severally.

2. M.A.No. 6376/2023 has been filed by the Insurance Company assailing the liability part of the impugned award; whereas, M.A.No. 7506/2023 has been filed on behalf of claimant seeking enhancement in the compensation amount.

3. Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 26/11/2020 at about 7.30 pm when claimant alongwith his wife was coming to Mohana Bus Stand by walking and reached near the scrap shop of one Shishupal Rathore, due to rash and negligent driving of motorcycle No. MP07MK3055 by its driver,
motorcycle dashed the claimant due to which he sustained grievous hurts in his head, forehead, leg National Insurance Company Limited vs Vikram Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100221404/
2 and other parts of the body, which gave rise to filing of claim case by the claimant under Section 166 of Motor Vehciles Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal seeking total compensation of Rs.
4,75,000/-; however, by the impugned award, learned Claims Tribunal awarded a compensation as mentioned hereinabove.

sentences.text: 4. It is the submission of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that learned Claims Tribunal erred in passing the impugned award against he evidence and pleadings brought on record.

The FIR was lodged on 20/12/2020 for an accident dated 26/11/2020 as such there was a delay of 24 days in lodging the FIR of which no satisfactory explanation has been offered even thereafter, Claims Tribunal by ignoring this aspect, passed the impugned award.

No accident took place by the offending vehicle, a motorcycle in the instant case by claimant in collision with police and driver &
owner of the offending motorcycle concocted a false story and got the motorcycle falsely implicated in the matter, just to claim compensation.
Though Insurance Company has specifically taken defence in this regard; however, ignoring the said learned Claims Tribunal passed the impugned award.

Further as per the admission record of J.A.Hopital, Gwalior, the accident occurred due to fall of complainant from the bike and in this regard, the Insurance Company has also examined, Dr.
Satyendra Singh; however, ignoring his statement, learned Claims Tribunal passed the impugned award.
No MLC of the date of accident has been annexed which is sufficient to show that matter has been cooked between claimant, police and owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the income of claimant as assessed by the Claims Tribunal is on lower side and the amount awarded under the other heads is also on lower side.

Learned claims Tribunal also erred in accepting the extent of permanent disability at 30%; whereas, as per disability certificate, Ex. P/47, claimant suffered permanent disability to the extent of 45% and accordinly prayed for enhancement of the compensation amount.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
7.

In the instant case, it is not in dispute that alleged accident is dated 26/11/2020 of which FIR was lodged on 20/12/2020 i.e. with a delay of 24 days and no sufficient explanation has been offerned for lodged the FIR with such a delay; whereas, claimant was discharged from hospital on 7/12/2020.

The claimant was taken to hospital at Mohana, JA hosital then Arogyadham, however, number of offending vehicle was not disclosed by him, it is for the first time at the time of lodging the FIR that the registration number of vehicle has been disclosed that too after a period of 25 days.

Further as per the case record of J.A. Hospital Gwalior, Ex. P/1, there is clear mention that claimant suffered injuries due to fall from bike at Mohana Bus Stand and such recital has been made on the basis of information given by the son of the claimant and this fact has been proved by Insurance Company by the evidence of Dr. Satyendra Singh Rajoriya.
There was no ground or basis of mentioning this fact wrongly in the case record.
As such first report about the accident is fall of claimant from the bike.

8. Further the evidence of the witnesses who have been produced on behalf of claimant to prove the factum of accident by the offending vehicle, there are material contradictions in their statement and same are not in the consonance with the report.

The mechanical report (Ex. P/11) also does not National Insurance Company Limited vs Vikram Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100221404/
3 support the version of the claimant.

sentences.text:
As such it is clear that the reason behind lodging the FIR with a huge delay was an afterthought to get the offending vehicle involved falsely in collusion with police,
owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
9. As such, it is clear that learned Claims Tribunal erred in passing the impugned award ignoring the material available on record.

Accordingly, while setting aside the impugned award, the appeal filed by Insurance Company vide M.A.No. 6376/2023 is allowed and since this Court finds that offending vehicle has been implanted in the accident and entire accident has been disbelieved, no case for enhancement of the compensation amount is made out, accordingly M.A.No.7506/2023 is hereby dismissed.

Parties to bear their own costs.
(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE jps/-
